tasks.short: Convert real objects into animation-ready models

steps.what: Prepare and optically scan the real object for modelling
Clean and model the scan into geometry suitable for animation
Check the model against the object and intended animated movement

tasks.design: Retain capture, topology cleanup, and movement-suitability checking in the scanning and modelling toolset {OTHER}. Native reconstruction already supports the workflow and is not a new source of labour savings.
tasks.previous_blocker: A scan may contain holes, reflections, or topology unsuitable for deformation.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional validated change is proposed beyond the existing toolset.
tasks.still_hard: Preserving the object's character while building geometry that deforms correctly.
tasks.human_edge: The artist judges where reconstruction errors matter visually and during movement.
tasks.altitude: Object capture and model-conversion responsibilities stay unchanged.

reach.task: Describe capture limitations that affect rigging

evidence.claim: Optical capture does not remove active preparation, model cleanup, or animation-readiness checks; no additional saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary covers conversion of a real object into an animation-ready model, excluding later shot animation and general visual concept design. OTHER is the existing optical-scanning and modelling toolset.
Artist produces the scan and capture observations in s1, then geometry in s2. Capture, scale checks, and cleanup remain fully counted; no ideal mesh or automated correctness flag is assumed.
Existing native reconstruction is the first choice. Unattended reconstruction runtime is outside human shares; retaining current tools adds zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Which scan defects cause the most active cleanup before the model can deform reliably?

incremental.description: No additional system or process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net saving zero. Existing reconstruction runtime is not active labour and the proposed process is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create pen-and-paper artwork for digital production

steps.what: Create pen-and-paper images suited to later scanning, editing, colouring, or animation

tasks.design: Retain the artist's paper drawing process and normal handover for digitisation. Requirements in {DOCS} can guide the artwork, but changing the medium would need evidence that it preserves the intended line and working method.
tasks.previous_blocker: The physical drawing process may be part of the desired artistic result.
tasks.enabler_now: No justified replacement of paper drawing is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Expressive line, composition, and anticipating how the image will be used digitally.
tasks.human_edge: The artist makes intentional marks and sees what needs changing before handover.
tasks.altitude: The artist retains the same drawing responsibilities.

reach.task: Explain the paper artwork's intended digital treatment
reach.learn: Scan resolution, separation, and handover conventions

evidence.claim: Digital image generation does not establish an equivalent replacement for intentional pen-and-paper artwork; no saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is creating paper originals for later digital treatment. Actual scanning, colouring, and animation occur after handover and are not invented baseline steps here.
Artist creates the original during s1; the project owner supplies the existing brief and handover requirements beforehand. No structured feed or new capture process is required.
Native drawing and document workflows remain sufficient; unchanged practice adds zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Whether the same artist also handles scanning
research_questions: Which qualities of the paper original must survive digitisation?

incremental.description: No new system or process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net saving zero. Original drawing stays unchanged and downstream digital work is outside this task boundary.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Set up models, constraints, and parameters for the intended animated behaviour
Inspect simulation trials and adjust object behaviour for the finished sequence
Check simulated behaviour for visual continuity and suitability in the finished sequence

tasks.design: Keep simulation setup, tuning, and shot-level review in the animation simulation application {OTHER}. Existing solver execution is already automated and does not justify reducing the artist's active shares.
tasks.previous_blocker: Numerically valid behaviour can look wrong or fail the intended shot.
tasks.enabler_now: No measured improvement to active simulation judgement is established in the digest.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing parameters that produce coherent and expressive movement across the sequence.
tasks.human_edge: The artist sees when a physical-looking result distracts from the intended action.
tasks.altitude: Simulation responsibility and creative decisions remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain an unstable simulation or shot-continuity constraint
reach.learn: Solver limits and reproducible scene setup

evidence.claim: Existing simulation execution does not remove active setup, tuning, and perceptual checking; no new labour saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary covers simulation-specific work, excluding general modelling, scanning, and ordinary keyframe animation. OTHER is the animation simulation application; overlapping scene work must be assigned once in a roll-up.

Artist produces constraints, parameter values, collision relationships and trial conditions in s1, then trial observations in s2. All active capture and tuning time stays counted; no acceptable-behaviour flag is presumed.
Native simulation tools remain the first choice. Solver runtime is outside active labour shares; unchanged tools require zero additional upkeep.
research_questions: Which active tuning operations repeat across shots and can be measured separately from solver runtime?

incremental.description: No additional system or process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving zero. Active setup, tuning, and shot review are unchanged; unattended simulation runtime is excluded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The artist retains physical capture, original drawing, and simulation judgement; existing software runtime is kept separate from labour.
role.ambitious_version: An artist who preserves the intended visual result through capture, paper-to-digital handover, and controlled simulation.
